# The audit tests

One test per item the site's audit found (a link, a header, a field, a page), each asking the site again what the audit
saw: 79 items, in `src/test/java/com/leotechnologies/tests/cases/audit/`, one file a finding code. They are rebuilt from the crawl;
a team adds none of its own (its checks are stories). Every suite has them, with its audit as AUDIT.md; a finding that
only an optional class of the build brings is in the audit and here only when the suite was built with that class.

## Running them

`mvn test -Dgroups=audit` runs them, and nothing else does: never a push, a pull request or the full run (the pipelines' audit job is
started by a person). Each item ends one of three ways:

- **skipped, "expected: still open"**: the site still shows it, as the audit said. This is no failure.
- **passed, "fixed, accepted"**: a person accepted it fixed, and it still is.
- **failed**: a surprise, which a person reads: an item seen FIXED and not yet accepted, one open again after its
  accept (REOPENED), one never seen open by this suite (NOT REPRODUCED), or a check that could not run.

The run ends "N of M audit items fixed since the audit of <date>", and how many of the audit's findings no test checks.
A run with every item still open passes: the exit code is not the deliverable; the last lines and audit/STATUS.md are.

## Showing a fix

1. Run the tests once before any fix, then `node menu/audit.mjs baseline`: the run is kept as the before
   (audit/runs/baseline-<stamp>.md). A pass counts as FIXED only for an item this suite has seen open.
2. After a fix, run them again: the item fails "FIXED: not yet accepted", naming the command.
3. `node menu/audit.mjs accept` takes every firm item the last run saw FIXED; `node menu/audit.mjs accept <id>` takes one,
   and is the only way to take a softer one (65 of these items are softer). The item leaves bugs/open/, a line joins bugs/FIXED.md,
   the run is kept in audit/runs/, and audit/STATUS.md is written again. Commit them: the record is a file in git.
4. `node menu/audit.mjs dismiss <id> --why "..."` marks a false finding or an accepted risk: it leaves the count and stays
   in audit/STATUS.md with who, when and why.

`node menu/audit.mjs status` says each item as the last run (`target/audit/run.json`) saw it, and writes audit/STATUS.md.

A **softer** check reports FIXED all the same, with "a softer check: confirm by eye": what it reads can move without the
finding changing (a page's words, a script's error that depends on timing, another site's answer), or it checks the first
pages of more. Look at the page before you accept one.

An item is fixed when the owner's own run of these tests against the live address says so. The run's result can be
edited by hand, so the proof is that anyone can run them again, not the file. A run against another address (a staging
copy) is refused by accept and baseline unless told (`--other-address`), and recorded so.

## Findings no test re-checks

- SITE-35: another site's hosts, as one machine's network sees them
- SITE-40: unconfirmed, and of another site or of no known source
